title.narrative: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Revenue Mobilization and Public Resource Management

description.narrative: The development objective of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) Revenue Mobilization and Public Resource Management Project for Pakistan is to increase the collection of KP's own source revenues (OSR) and improve the management of public Resources. The Government of KP (GoKP's) public financial management reform strategy (PFMRS) covers the whole PFM cycle at the provincial and local government (LG) levels. The strategy is organized around six objectives: (a) ensuring policy-driven planning and budgeting; (b) facilitating a comprehensive, credible, and transparent annual budget; (c) improving predictability and control in budget execution; (d) enabling resource mobilization and enhancing provincial OSR; (e) improving asset and liability management; and (f) fostering accountability for results. The program is divided into two parts: part one, program-for-results and part two, investment project financing.
To increase the collection of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's own source revenues and improve the management of public resources

condition.narrative: Establish, by no later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, and thereafter maintain throughout the period ofimplementation of the Operation, a Shared Services Unit (“SSU”) and an Operation Support Unit (“OSU”)within FD, which units shallbe: (i) headed by a director (SSU)/Operation coordinator (OSU), assisted by experienced and qualified staff, in adequate numbers,under terms of reference satisfactory to the Association; and (ii) shall be responsible for carrying out financial management,procurement and manage environmental and social safeguards (SSU in coordination with OSU)/the implementation of the Operation (OSUin coordination with the SSU)."

For purpose of verifying the achievement of the DLRs, engage, not later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, anindependent third-party entity or entities (the “Third-Party Independent Verification Agent”), with qualifications, experience andterms of reference satisfactory to the Association, to undertake the verification process.

Maintain, throughout the period of implementation of the Operation, a working group (“Reform Working Group”), comprised ofofficials of various government entities, in adequate numbers and under terms of reference satisfactory to the Association, vestedwith the responsibility of overseeing the implementation of the Operation in their respective agencies.

Undertake, at least semi-annually, through the Third-Party Verification Agent, a verification process, in a manner and substancesatisfactory to the Association, and pursuant to the verification protocol agreed with the Association, to ascertain the ProgramImplementing Entity's achievement/fulfillment of Disbursement-Linked Results during the period under review.

title.narrative: Registered taxpayers who filed GSTS in previous year

comment.narrative: As per updated IVA report, KPRA has achieved filing compliance of 72% for FY24. TPV report on the achievement of target for FY25 will be shared by December 2025.

title.narrative: Share of ADP funds spent on capital investment

comment.narrative: In FY2022/23, total Annual Development Plan (ADP) was PKR 283 billion (excluding foreign funded projects) and the amount for capital share was PKR 230.23billion or 81.35% of total ADP. In FY2023/24 this share has increased to 82% based on total ADP of PKR 74billion and capital share of PKR 60 billion (updated data). As a result, program-end target has been achieved. In FY2024/25, the share of capital investments in ADP was 80% (capital allocation is PKR175 billion out of total ADP of PKR 220 billion), while 81% is planned for FY2025/26.

baseline.value: No linkages among KP tax authorities databases or with third-parties

target.value: A shared data warehouse for KP tax authorities is operational, providing shared data access to KP tax authorities, accessible through taxpayers name, CNIC number or other defined fields.

comment.narrative: The KP's Cabinet approved the data integration plan in January 2021, following which the KP Revenue Authority (KPRA) successfully established linkages with four withholding agents: KP Information Technology Board, MOL, Water and Sanitation Services Peshawar, and Accountant General of KP. In FY23, the tax authorities confirmed readiness for database integration, and an action plan was agreed upon with the tax authorities to simplify and digitize business processes. A tax database integration framework and business requirement document have been developed. The integrated tax data is housed at KPRA's data center. Data connectivity between KPRA and BOR has been established, and dashboard designed. Digitization and integration of data for key taxes within BOR and ETNCD is ongoing – after which data linkage with ETNCD will be completed. This will enable tax entities to view and exchange data to expand tax base.

actual.value: BoR and ETNCD are in the process of automating their tax records and databases. Data integration framework, business requirement document and dashboards have been developed.

title.narrative: TMAs using FMIS to record transactions

target.value: Provided that the 30 TMAs continue to use FMIS to record payments:20 additional TMAs have used the FMIS to record payments throughout Year 5

comment.narrative: FMIS Decentralization Plan was approved by the government, and Access System was developed, tested, and rolled-out. As per last third party report, 127 Tehsil Municipal Authorities (TMAs) were using FMIS to manage their budget and record transactions. The number of TMAs using FMIS is reported to have increased to 130 as per the information shared by the department. A sustainability and further expansion plan has been prepared for the system based on a recent review of the system. As part of this plan, updated modules have also been rolled out, and helpdesk is being established for continuous support to field offices. Going forward, the FMIS will be hosted and managed at KP data center.

actual.value: As per final TPV report, 130 TMAs are using FMIS.

title.narrative: Business processes for tax administration simplified and digitized

baseline.value: Key tax administration processes are not simplified and digitized for main taxes

target.value: Taxpayer registration, filing or invoicing, payment, monitoring of arrears and appeals processes of key taxes digitized

comment.narrative: KPRA has finalized its registration portal, while sales tax returns e-filing continues using PRAL system (and single portal). Online payment of tax facility is also available. BOR's key initiatives include the simplification of land registration, land mutations, issuance of Fard (through service delivery centers), online registration, filing and payment of agriculture income tax, and the collection of stamp duties through the e-stamp system and Service Delivery Centres (SDCs). The E&T department introduced online payment and registration system for Motor Vehicle tax. Property tax record is digitized in 10 cities, while the same is being digitized in additional cities.

actual.value: BOR and ETNCD are in the process of automating their tax databases and tax admin business processes, while KPRA has digitized registration, filing, and payment of sales tax.

title.narrative: E-Government functionality strengthened in selected government departments

baseline.value: Limited and uneven functionality of e-Government

target.value: Implementation of e archiving/indexing of government records in at least three targeted departments

comment.narrative: - GovKP has approved e-Gov strategy and implementation plan - Business process mapping and plan completed for selected business processes. Digitization completed for selected processes under tranche 1 (related with leadership and direction, project appraisals, and regulations). The digitized modules of key business processes have been rolledout for mandatory usage by all government departments. - Focal persons and master trainers of all administrative departments have been notified, and training provided to staff covering more than 600 functional users of the system. Additional training being provided as new modules of the system are being rolled out. - User credentials and Email IDs were created for user of digitized processes, and user management system have been developed manage the hierarchies during transfer /postings - Procurement of hardware and software for data center completed. Procurement of wireless points in process. Firm contract updated for remaining modules.

actual.value: Development of digitized modules for selected business processes has completed, and is being reviewed. But some modules are pending, and e-Archiving is yet to be initiated. Some trainings have been provided to departments.

title.narrative: Improved capacity for revenue generation from public property

baseline.value: No asset maps of government-owned real estate.

target.value: A pilot for commercial utilization of public real estate successfully completed

comment.narrative: The BOR has digitized record of asset maps for some areas with the support of Survey of Pakistan. The record is being verified by the BOR team. However, a consistent approach is needed to complete this work, as well as to review legal framework and design performance framework for revenue generation from public property.

actual.value: No further progress on digitizing asset maps; the work on improving legal and performance framework was not initiated.

title.narrative: Cities with updated UIPT surveys and digitized records

baseline.value: No recent survey conducted; partial digitization of tax records in some cities.

target.value: Update property valuations in at least one city

comment.narrative: Target of completing the work in 10 cities has been achieved – as verified by third party. These include Havelian, Nowshera Kallan, Pabbi, Akora Khattak, Amangarh, Jahangira, Abbottabad, Katlang, Lachi and Shakardara. The government is working on a plan to shift to capital value for property taxes, for which legal changes have been proposed. After the approval of the law, they plan to conduct the pilot for updating property valuation.

actual.value: Activities for updating property valuations are ongoing.

baseline.value: No reports currently published; No estimate of pension liabilities

target.value: Annual reports for KP Funds published

comment.narrative: - A draft of Systems for Fund Administration (SFA) bill was prepared, as part of efforts to design the institutional framework for funds management. However, the bill was not approved. Funds management policy was also not approved. - The actuarial study was completed about pension liability (amounting to RS.3 trillion), and a report on pension fund (PF) liabilities was published in FY22, as reported by Finance Department. However, reports on assets investment portfolio & liabilities of GPIF and PF are not published annually.

actual.value: KP funds reports are not published.

title.narrative: ADP funds allocated to unapproved projects (except foreign project assistance)

baseline.value: Allocated funds to unapproved projects are 49% of total ADP(excluding Foreign project assistance)in FY18.

target.value: DLR 5.5: Allocated funds to Unapproved Projects have not exceeded 20% of total ADP (excluding Foreign Project Assistance) in FY24

comment.narrative:
The program-end target has been achieved, as verified by third party. Percentage of ADP funds allocated to new projects that have not been approved by the competent authority, has reduced to 15% during FY24. Out of total 2,196 projects, 317 new projects/schemes were unapproved. Total PKR 10. 866 billion were allocated to these unapproved projects, which is 15% of total ADP allocation of PKR 73.576 billion (excluding foreign aid).
In FY25, allocation to new schemes was Rs. 36.84 billion, which is around 17% of total ADP allocation of Rs.220 billion.

title.narrative: OBB departments with measurable gender KPIs, reporting number of females reached by their services

comment.narrative: Year 1: 25%, 8 out of 32 departments; Year 2, 3, and 4: 28%, 9 out of 33 departments; and Year 5: 26%, 9 out of 34 departments (recently the Govt of KP increased the number of departments from 32 to 34). These 9 departments have gender based KPIs (55 indicators) and they report number of females reached by their services. It is important to develop KPIs for and build capacity of additional departments in this area so that relevant reporting can be done on regular basis. As per recent information shared by the Government of KP, 34 departments are following the OBB guidelines under OBB 2025-28.

Total 3 departments (Social welfare, Relief & Rehabilitation and Education departments) have submitted their sector plans. Govt of KP has implemented PAMframes tool across all departments to track the output and outcome of Public Investment Management.

title.narrative: Cash management based on regular consolidation of cash balances and cash plans

baseline.value: Cash management not based on regular consolidation of cash balances and regular cash plans.

target.value: At least 4 Govt Departments, whose cash balances are daily consolidated, have prepared monthly cash plans and submitted to FD

comment.narrative: A cash management committee of the Finance Department (FD) worked with the international consultant on revised cash management policy and implementation plan - which has been approved. A cash management unit has been established in FD, and cash plans received from two departments, while training on cash forecasting and planning are being provided to the selected departments, whose cash consolidation will be initiated soon.

actual.value: A revised cash management policy has been approved; cash management unit established, cash plans received from two departments, and training being provided to two departments to initiate consolidation and forecasting.

title.narrative: Increase in own source tax revenues (USD million)

comment.narrative:
Revision: Considering improved performance of KP Government in revenue mobilization, OSR targets included for extended period of Program (5% increase each year), using FY24 as baseline (USD 202mn).
As per final collections data, KP collected tax revenues of Rs. 54 billion (or US$ 190 million) from own sources in FY24. The province's tax collections in FY25 was Rs. 70 billion (revised estimate) or USD 248 million, against the target of USD 212 million.

title.narrative: Cash deposits held by Government in commercial banks

baseline.value: Rs. 105 billion in 723 accounts of autonomous bodies and mainstream government departments, held in commercial banks (Dec 2023)

target.value: Consolidating at least 50% (over baseline) of the balances of government accounts held in commercial banks.

comment.narrative:
Revision: Targets revised to align with government's revised methodology of balance sweeping arrangement for daily consolidation of cash balances.
As per latest report from State Bank of Pakistan (June 2025), cash balances held by the KP Government in commercial banks amounted to Rs. 513 billion (389% increase over revised baseline of Rs. 105billion in Dec 2023). Total accounts maintained in commercial banks were 80,486. However, recently, the Government of KP approved revised cash management policy, and established a Cash Management Unit in the Finance Department to support these reforms. Cash forecasting and planning related training is being provided to selected line departments, for whom cash consolidation using sweeping approach is to be initiated.

actual.value: Not achieved. PKR 513 billion cash balances held in commercial banks (389% increase over revised baseline of Rs. 105billion in Dec 2023). Revised cash management policy approved, cash management unit established. But cash consolidation has not started yet.
